event: 2025 ILCA 4 YOUTH EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS & OPEN EUROPEAN TROPHY
procedural_matters: On 23 June, twenty two (22) boats of the ILCA 4 Girls Gold fleet, delivered requests for redress, alleging an improper action of the race committee in race F1.
The international jury decided to call a hearing to consider redress for all the boats of the ILCA 4 Girls gold fleet.

Hearing No. 58 was heard together with hearings No. 32,33,34,35,37,38,39,41,42,43,44,45,47,48,49,50,51,53,54,55,56, and 57 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since all hearings arose from the same incident.

A list of all boats called to the hearing can be seen in the file attached under the names 'ATTENDEES'. In that list, the ticked boats were present during the hearing and were represented by their respective sailors.
The following boats did not attend the hearing: ESP 211117, FIN 226893, ITA 222729, ITA 222844, ITA 226941, SWE
The hearing proceeded in their absence, in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
The race committee was represented by Ewa Jodlowska (Course Race Officer Area A).

The following coaches attended the hearing as observers: Wannes Van Laer (BEL), Erik Voets (NED), James Parker- Mowbray (GBR), Jakub Lawicki (POL), Pierre Gueguen (FRA), Alfred Fengheh (MLT), Nikolaos Chrysos (GRE), Alexios Katsios (GRE), Joaquin Cores (ESP), Borja Mas (ESP), Antonio Petroli (ITA), Antonio Russo (ITA), and Patrick Paul (GER).
The coaches of BEL, NED, GER, and some coaches from GRE attended the hearing on behalf of their sailors when giving the decision.
facts: Before the start of race F1 of the ILCA 4 Girls Gold fleet, the race committee had wind readings between 015 and 030 degrees.
The course was set with an axis of 020 degrees and that information was displayed on a board on the race committee signal vessel on the starting line.
The course to be sailed for the ILCA 4 Girls Gold fleet was O2 (Outer loop trapezoid course) that consists of 6 legs.
On leg 4 of the course (second upwind on the outer loop), while the 3rd boat was rounding mark 2, the race committtee noticed that the windmills ashore had turned facing west.
Shortly after, the wind on the course shifted, approximately 80 degrees to the left. The wind readings were between 290 and 300 degrees. At that moment 15 boats had rounded mark 2.
The race committee considered shortening the course. This was not possible as boats in the top part of the fleet had already rounded the mark and were sailing on the next leg of the course.

From the moment the wind shifted, the race committee was monitoring the boats and the race course, and was aware that a part of the fleet was reaching towards the next mark (3p), and other parts of the fleet had to sail on a reach or even wider towards mark 2.
The race committee did not display flag N.

Upon returning to shore, the race committee checked the GPS tracking of a random sample of boats (3 boats), focusing on boats that had delivered a request for redress. The places of those boats were not affected by the windshift.
The race committee did not abandon the race.
conclusions: By considering the influence of the windshift on the race, the race committee did not make an improper action or omission in not abbandoning the race.
Since the windshift did not affect directly the fairness of the competition, the race committee did not make an improper action or omission in non abbandoning the race.
There was neither an improper action nor improper omission of the race committee. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
